counterfactual_missing_items: No CRP result yet, so the LRINEC score is not final
No mention of bullae, skin necrosis, or crepitus on examination
No surgical/pathologic confirmation of fascial necrosis
decisive_items: Pelvic CT imaging demonstrated an ulceration of the left labia with air in the subcutaneous fat of the left groin and lower abdominal wall, as well as inflammatory fat stranding along the left lateral abdominal wall
Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotizing Fasciitis (LRINEC) score was calculated as 3, with the potential to rise to 7 pending C-reactive protein results
response.rationale: R4 is anchored by specific raw findings of subcutaneous gas, CT air in the groin and abdominal wall, and a LRINEC score prompting immediate surgery, all pointing to necrotizing fasciitis. R1 relies on nonspecific systemic signs such as hypotension and leukocytosis plus the phrase 'concerns for sepsis,' which is a downstream complication rather than the most likely localized diagnosis.

rejected.why: Sepsis is a systemic complication of the underlying soft-tissue infection; its raw spans are nonspecific and do not account for the localized subcutaneous gas, LRINEC score, or surgical indication.
